question: A 55-year-old Caucasian male presents for a routine colonoscopy. A polyp is found in the patient's transverse colon and is found to be cancerous on histological evaluation. Upon examination, it is found that these cancerous cells have decreased MHC class I expression on their surface. Which immune system cell is most capable of killing these tumor cells?
analysis: Natural killer (NK) cells are part of the innate immune system and are particularly effective at targeting and killing cells with decreased MHC class I expression. Tumor cells often downregulate MHC class I molecules to evade detection by cytotoxic T-cells, which rely on MHC class I to recognize and kill target cells. NK cells, however, can detect this downregulation and are activated to kill such cells. Therefore, in this scenario, NK cells are the most capable of killing the tumor cells with decreased MHC class I expression.
